concept.title: Table and tree
concept.shortdesc: The Table / Tree switch above the list changes how the project is drawn; the choice stays in the page's address (?view=), so a link or a reload keeps it. The type tabs (All, Requirement, Test Case, …) show one type at a time in either, with a count beside each.

ul.li: Table — the document's hierarchy, one dense row per artifact, every artifact nested under the heading or parent it sits in, with guide lines showing where it sits. The caret beside a heading or a parent folds and unfolds what is under it. Headings carry the same columns as every other row: the ref and title, the review status, the priority attribute, the quality score, trace (↑ how many artifacts this one answers to, ↓ how many answer to it, and ⚠ when one of those links is suspect), V&V below (the verification rollup: a green dot passes, red fails, orange is blocked, grey is not run or not covered; for a heading or a parent it rolls up the requirements under it, as passing/total) and how long ago it was updated.
Tree — the project drawn as a diagram of connected boxes (see The tree diagram).

conbody.p: The fold all / unfold all button beside the search folds every branch of the view in front, so only the top level shows, or opens every level; it turns to the other one each time you press it. Hover over it to see which it will do.

The figures above the list count what is in view: artifacts, the share traced (with at least one link), the share verified (requirements whose verification passes), suspect links and quality findings.

On a phone the list's views are chips under the search box: List (two lines per artifact: ref, status and age, then the title, then quality, trace and verification) and Outline (the hierarchy, one line per artifact, with the fold all / unfold all button beside the chips). The chips In review, Failing and Suspect narrow the list to what needs you.
Older links to the Layers view open the tree diagram, which shows the same levels and their verification at a glance.
